newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Qantas, JAL plan codesharing.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Qantas, JAL plan codesharing.

text.p: Qantas Airways Ltd said on Monday that it and Japan Airlines (JAL) proposed to rearrange and codeshare their flights from Queensland to Tokyo, subject to Australian government approval.
Under the deal, JAL would handle traffic for both airlines from Tokyo to Brisbane with daily flights, Qantas said in a statement.
Qantas would fly all of the Tokyo-to-Cairns services, again with daily flights.
Qantas would retain one weekly Tokyo-to-Brisbane flight as part of an existing Sydney service that stops at Brisbane.
A Qantas spokesman said the codeshare agreement did not cover the Sydney-Brisbane-Tokyo service.

"There would be no reduction in the number of seats available for sale on both airlines on the 14 codeshare flights between Tokyo and Cairns and between Tokyo and Brisbane," Qantas said in the statement.
Each airline currently flies seven weekly Tokyo services with 747s landing at both Cairns and Brisbane.
The codeshare services would also be flown by 747s.
However, the Sydney-Brisbane-Tokyo service would be downgraded to a 767, replacing the current 747 schedule.
Codesharing means that each airline sells tickets on the service as if it were its own.
